# Results — Study 676 (Gator Oscillator)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
Gator Oscillator (the convergence/divergence of Bill Williams' Alligator's three
smoothed moving averages) tells you when a trend "sleeps" vs "eats"; trade when the
gator wakes**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month).
Fingerprints `7b64d4cd54dd` (30-name basket, wide close panel) / `eed0b5d1f41e` (SPY
OHLC, the timer instrument).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` (split/dividend-adjusted total-return), 30 names — SPY + 29 long-listed liquid US large-caps — 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (6,662 sessions) |
| Basket | **survivors basket** (every name still trades in 2026) — the same 30-name shape used by sibling studies [402-engulfing-pattern](../../402-engulfing-pattern/) / [421-williams-alligator](../../421-williams-alligator/). Named on the Signal axis: a fixed surviving-names basket cannot include firms delisted after a bad run |
| Indicator | Jaw/Teeth/Lips = SMMA(13/8/5) of the median price `(H+L)/2`, forward-shifted 8/5/3 bars — **identical construction to sibling [421-williams-alligator](../../421-williams-alligator/)**. Gator upper = \|Jaw−Teeth\|, lower = \|Teeth−Lips\|; a bar is GREEN if taller than the prior bar, RED otherwise |
| Event ("wake") | the first bar where **both** histograms flip red→green together, immediately after **≥ 3** consecutive both-red ("sleeping") bars (`MIN_SLEEP = 3`, fixed once, reused everywhere — not tuned for a result). A single-day flip with no prior sleep is common (~24% of days) and is not what the folklore calls "waking" |
| Statistics | HAC (Newey-West) one-sample *t* on the signed post-wake forward return, Welch *t* vs the unconditional base rate, a 5,000-draw label-shuffle placebo (event study); a 2,000-draw circular-block-permutation placebo (timer) |
| Execution / costs | **one documented lag**: the wake/fan state is known at the close of bar *t*; the event study enters the **next bar's open** (t+1) and the timer enters the **next bar's return** (t+1). One-way costs × NAV per leg (5 / 10 bps swept), 50 bps/yr borrow on the timer's short leg, flat 4%/yr cash-leg proxy when the timer is out of the market (FRED unavailable offline — same proxy as [421](../../421-williams-alligator/)) |
| Data quirks (named) | `MIN_SLEEP = 3` is a genuine modeling decision (without it, "wake" fires on ~24% of days — any local minimum of two correlated noisy series — which is not the claim); the timer's raw Sharpe is inflated by a cash-dominance artifact (see the Tradability section) — the decisive numbers are the Sharpe-**difference** HAC *t* and the block-permutation placebo, not the raw Sharpe |

No survivorship on the *indicator* construction itself (it only reads OHLC); the
**basket is a survivors panel**, named above per house rule.

## The headline — wake-event forward returns vs the unconditional base rate

346 wake events pooled across the 30-name basket; 192 of them (120 bullish fan, 72
bearish fan) sit inside an ordered Alligator fan and get a directional sign — the other
154 wake with the three lines *not* cleanly ordered and are excluded from the signed
test (they still count in the magnitude test below). Enter the next bar's open, signed
long on a bullish fan / short on a bearish fan.

| H (days) | n wake | n signed | bull | bear | mean signed | unconditional | win % | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5bps) |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 346 | 192 | 120 | 72 | **+0.013%** | +0.030% | 52.1% | −0.17 | +0.13 | 0.468 | −0.088% |
| 5 | 346 | 192 | 120 | 72 | −0.009% | +0.233% | 49.5% | −1.09 | −0.04 | 0.510 | −0.114% |
| **10** | 346 | 192 | 120 | 72 | **−0.119%** | **+0.479%** | 46.9% | **−1.88** | −0.40 | 0.634 | −0.229% |
| 20 | 346 | 192 | 120 | 72 | +0.604% | +0.976% | 51.0% | −0.73 | +1.35 | 0.136 | +0.484% |

At every horizon the signed post-wake return is **indistinguishable from zero** (HAC
*t* never exceeds ±1.35) and **indistinguishable from the unconditional base rate**
(Welch *t* never exceeds ±1.88, always below the ±2 bar). The 10-day horizon — the same
window the timer below trades — has the largest (negative) point estimate and it still
misses the bar. No horizon shows a directional edge, gross or net.

## Trend-capture (magnitude, not direction) — does a wake predict a BIGGER move?

The believer's fallback: maybe the Gator doesn't call direction, but it flags that
*something is coming*. Tested directly: mean \|forward return\| after any wake (346
events, both directional and non-directional) vs the unconditional mean \|forward
return\| on the same names.

| H (days) | mean \|ret\| after wake | unconditional \|ret\| | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 1.001% | 1.043% | −0.83 | 0.743 |
| 5 | 2.497% | 2.645% | −1.20 | 0.842 |
| **10** | **3.364%** | **3.785%** | **−2.41** | 0.977 |
| 20 | 5.169% | 5.431% | −0.99 | 0.809 |

If anything the 10-day move **after** a wake is *smaller* than average (Welch *t* =
−2.41) — the opposite of "trend capture." It is one horizon out of four (not a robust
pattern across the window, and the label-shuffle placebo assigns it no special
standing — p = 0.977, i.e. a random pick this quiet is unremarkable), so the honest
read is "no magnitude edge either way," not "the Gator predicts calm." Either way, the
"bigger move coming" folklore has nothing to stand on here.

## Third axis / Tradability — a real timer on SPY

Enter the fan direction the bar after a wake, hold **10 sessions** (matching the
event-study horizon above), one execution lag, 5 bps one-way costs + 50 bps/yr borrow
on shorts, flat 4%/yr cash-leg proxy while flat (2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30, SPY only).

| strategy | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol (ann.) | Max DD | *t* (mean ≠ 0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold | **+8.28%** | +0.412 | 19.32% | −55.2% | +2.42 |
| Gator-wake timer | +4.26% | **+2.548** | 1.64% | −5.7% | +15.22 |
| "Always in the fan" (421-style) | +2.26% | +0.126 | 17.69% | −37.5% | +0.75 |

The wake timer's raw Sharpe (+2.548) looks spectacular next to buy-and-hold's +0.412 —
and it is a **mirage of arithmetic, not skill**: the timer is out of the market
**99.1%** of the time (only **13 wake events on SPY in 26.5 years** clear the fan
filter), earning a smooth, near-zero-volatility 4%/yr cash proxy on almost every day, so
its *annualized volatility collapses to 1.64%* and the Sharpe ratio explodes — a classic
case of "normalise before you marvel" (a strategy that is 99% cash by construction will
always print an inflated Sharpe against a 100%-equity benchmark; the ratio says nothing
about skill). The numbers that matter:

- **Sharpe-difference HAC *t* (wake vs buy-and-hold): −1.16** — the timer's advantage
  is **not statistically distinguishable from zero**, despite the Sharpe headline. It
  also earns *half* buy-and-hold's CAGR (+4.26% vs +8.28%) in absolute terms.
- **Sharpe-difference HAC *t* (wake vs the plain "always in the fan" rule): +0.65** —
  not significant either. Watching the histogram change color adds nothing measurable
  over simply knowing the fan is bullish or bearish.
- **Circular-block-permutation placebo (2,000 draws): p = 0.512.** A random reshuffle
  of the *same sparse in/out exposure pattern* beats buy-and-hold's Sharpe by this much
  or more **51% of the time** — the "amazing Sharpe" is exactly what a mostly-cash
  strategy looks like by chance, not a timing edge.
- **13 events in 26.5 years** is not a strategy — it is a curiosity with no meaningful
  trading frequency or capacity, and the result is unchanged at 10 bps costs (CAGR
  +4.23%, Sharpe +2.531): with this few trades, costs were never going to be the story.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A trend-persistence knob (`edge`), identical in spirit to sibling 421: multi-week
directional regimes whose strength scales with `edge`. Each "panel" pools 20
independent synthetic series (the synthetic analogue of the real 30-name basket) so the
wake-event detector has enough pooled events to compute a meaningful *t*, exactly as the
real basket does.

| world | n wake | n signed | mean signed | Welch *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge=0`), **10 seeds** | 95–121/panel | 51–66/panel | ≈ 0 | — | mean **+0.41** (sd 0.78), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/10 seeds** |
| planted `edge=8.0` (seed 676) | 14 | 14 | **+7.02%** | **+2.54** | **+3.20** |

The detector never fires on the null across 10 independent panel draws and clears the
bar decisively on a planted multi-week trend — the machinery works; it simply finds
nothing on the real tape. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The signed post-wake forward return clears **|t| ≥ 2** at **no**
  horizon (1/5/10/20 days) on either the HAC or the Welch test, and the label-shuffle
  placebo never rejects the null. The magnitude ("trend-capture") claim fares no
  better — the one horizon that shows anything (10 days, Welch *t* = −2.41) points the
  **wrong way**: calmer, not louder.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A real SPY timer's headline Sharpe (+2.548) is a
  cash-dominance artifact from sitting out 99.1% of the time — the Sharpe-difference
  HAC *t* vs buy-and-hold is only −1.16, vs the plain "always in the fan" rule only
  +0.65, and a block-permutation placebo shows the same or a better Sharpe advantage
  from a random reshuffle of the same sparse exposure **51% of the time**. Thirteen
  trades in 26.5 years carries no meaningful capacity either way.
- **"Does the gator's awakening catch the start of a trend?" — BUSTED.** The synthetic
  control proves the *machinery* can catch a genuine planted trend (*t* = +3.20 on
  `edge=8.0`); on the real tape it catches nothing directional and, if anything, the
  "big move ahead" story runs backwards at the one horizon that shows any hint of
  significance.
